sections.h2: How a Willingboro sale differs from most New Jersey sales
sections.html:
Before ownership of a Willingboro house can change, the township wants to issue a certificate of occupancy, and the inspection has to be booked a full 15 days before settlement. That lead time drives the whole schedule: heating certification, any repairs, a possible recheck, then the deed filing in Mount Holly.

Willingboro is a Burlington County suburb of Philadelphia with 32,824 residents. Below you will find local housing numbers, the resale inspection rules, deed and tax steps, and how an agent, a sale on your own and a cash buyer compare.

Willingboro grew out of one builder's plan, and the numbers still show it. Owners live in 84.3 percent of homes, households average 3.02 people, and the township packs about 4,128 people into each of its 7.73 square miles of land. The 2020 count was 31,889.

sections.h2: Levittown neighborhoods and how buyers search
sections.html:
Levitt and Sons built its third and largest Levittown here in the 1950s and 1960s. The first homes sold in June 1958, and the population jumped from 852 in 1950 to 43,386 in 1970. Voters briefly renamed the place Levittown Township in 1959 and went back to Willingboro in a November 1963 referendum. The planning left a pattern buyers still use:

  • Neighborhoods are called parks, such as Pennypacker Park, Millbrook Park, Windsor Park and Hawthorne Park.
  • Streets in each park begin with the park's initial, so a Pennypacker address starts with P.
  • Country Club Ridge was laid out around a golf course in the 1960s.
  • Pennypacker Park and Country Club Park hold the community pools.

Many houses came from a small set of Levitt floor plans, so a buyer can often compare yours with the same model a few streets over. Mention additions and the age of the roof and furnace when you present the house.

U.S. Route 130 forms the northwest edge of the township, and Rancocas Creek drains the southwest side. Of 122.11 miles of road, 109.02 are township-maintained. Transit is by bus: NJ Transit routes 409, 417 and 418 run between Trenton and Philadelphia, BurLink operates two local routes, and Academy Bus connects to Midtown and Lower Manhattan.

Willingboro Township Public Schools covers Hawthorne, W.R. James Sr. and Twin Hills for grades 1 to 4, Levitt Intermediate for grades 5 and 6, Memorial Middle School for 7 and 8, and Willingboro High School. Families will ask which school serves your park, so find out before the first showing.

Chapter 199 of the township code, the housing standards chapter, bars a change of ownership or occupancy until the Department of Inspections issues a certificate of occupancy. The ordinance sets these steps:

  • The owner or agent applies and pays the fee in the township fee schedule.
  • The visit must be scheduled at least 15 calendar days before settlement, and a request made within four days of it adds an $80 expedite charge.
  • Cancel or move the appointment with a day's notice, or the first fee is charged regardless.
  • The inspector makes a visual check of accessible parts of the structure, which does not guarantee the electrical, plumbing or heating systems.
  • A qualified technician authorized by the township must separately certify the heating equipment, and that certification can be no more than 30 days old when the certificate issues.
  • If the house fails, the department sends a written list of defects, and the owner has 30 days from the visit to repair them and ask for a recheck.

Call the Department of Inspections for the current fee and application steps. If the buyer will take on repairs, write that into the contract so both sides know who pays.

sections.h2: Filing the deed and state fees
sections.html:
The Burlington County Clerk's main office, 50 Rancocas Road in Mount Holly, accepts deeds on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The clerk also offers a free Property Fraud Alert service that flags any document filed under your name.

One paperwork rule is new. County staff reject any GIT/REP seller declaration signed on or after October 1, 2025 that is not on the latest state form.

For prices up to $350,000 the state's realty transfer fee is $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, then $3.35 per $500 through $200,000, then $3.90 per $500 through $350,000. Your closing agent will confirm the exact figure for your price.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and the October tax sale
sections.html:
Bills follow the calendar year, with installments due on the first of February, May, August and November and a ten-day grace period after each. From the eleventh day, interest is figured back to the first, and a postmark earns no credit.

Pay at the window in the municipal building, the Police Department drop box, by mail or on the township's online portal. The tax office is in Suite 205 at One Rev. Dr. M. L. King Jr. Drive, with window hours from 9 in the morning to 4:30. The portal rejects prior-year balances, so get an exact payoff figure from the collector before closing.

Earlier unpaid taxes and municipal charges still open after December 31 go into the township's electronic tax sale, held each October. Senior, veteran and disabled-person deductions are handled by the assessor's office at 609-877-2200.

sections.h2: Agent, own sale or cash buyer?
sections.html:
A listing can bring the strongest price for a clean house, a cash buyer removes the repair cycle, and selling alone falls between them. Timing is the real difference, because of the 15-day inspection lead.

  • An agent suits a house in good repair that can pass inspection without a long defect list.
  • A solo sale suits an owner who follows recent prices in the neighborhood and will hire an attorney for the contract.
  • A cash purchase suits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate, since the buyer can take over the defect list.

Book the township inspection the moment a closing date exists, and measure each offer by the cash that reaches you after transfer fee, taxes and payoff.

Work backward from the closing date. First, set the township inspection at least 15 calendar days ahead, since a late request costs $80 more. Next, hire the technician who will certify the heating equipment, remembering that the certification can be no more than 30 days old. If the inspector lists defects, you have 30 days to fix them and ask for a recheck, so a sale with many repairs needs more room on the calendar.

In parallel, ask the tax collector for a payoff figure, request a lender payoff if a mortgage remains, and make sure the seller declaration is on the current state form. Then your closing agent files the deed in Mount Holly. A cash buyer who agrees to take the house as is can absorb the defect list, which skips the recheck step.

faqs.q: Is an inspection mandatory before a Willingboro sale?
faqs.a: Yes. A certificate of occupancy is needed before ownership changes, and the visit must be booked 15 calendar days ahead. A qualified technician must also certify the heating equipment.

faqs.q: What if the inspector finds defects?
faqs.a: The department issues a written notice of defects. You have 30 days from the inspection to finish repairs and request a reinspection, and the certificate follows once the house passes.

faqs.q: What are the Willingboro installment dates?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, each followed by ten grace days. Postmarks are ignored, and balances still open after December 31 enter the October tax sale.

faqs.q: Which office records a Willingboro deed?
faqs.a: The Burlington County Clerk's main office, 50 Rancocas Road in Mount Holly, which serves the public on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Can a Willingboro house with tenants or repair needs be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The certificate rules still apply, but an as-is buyer can agree to take over the defect list and the occupancy. Spell out who handles the inspection and repairs in the contract.
